title: A pass that dispatches a worker outlives its own publish slot
description:
The first cloud run to get a worker all the way through its tick could not record the result:

    plan-1   6:34:39 -> 6:41:39   7 minutes   ERROR
    Error: the repository publisher refused the write: no publish slot is held for
    pengelbrecht/ticks, so nothing may publish to it (the publish slot is held by run nobody)

    publish-slot-1 acquired_at 04:34:38Z  expires_at 04:37:38Z   (3 minute TTL)

The pass took seven minutes and the slot lasted three. The publish at the end was refused by the room, correctly - the run no longer held the slot it was writing under.

This is the same SHAPE as 0h9 and a different cause. 8xd made the tracker read 137 ms, so the read is no longer what makes a pass long. What makes it long now is the work: this pass dispatched a worker, the worker deleted two files and wrote its report, and that took about seven minutes of wall clock. That is not an anomaly, it is what a pass IS.

Mechanism: the slot is renewed ONCE, at the start of the pass, before reconcilePass() runs (epic-reconciler.ts, the renewal sits above the pass call). Nothing renews it while the pass is in flight. A three-minute lease renewed once cannot cover a pass whose length is set by a model doing work.

The worker's output was not lost - it is on refs/heads/tick/uzc/attempt-1/f8l, two commits, correct. The run simply cannot write down that it happened.

Fix shape, and the choice matters:
- Renew the slot DURING the pass, on a cadence well inside the TTL, not once at its start. The lease exists to say a live run holds the repository; a heartbeat is what makes that true, and a run that stops heartbeating should lose the slot.
- Do NOT simply lengthen the TTL. A longer TTL means a dead run wedges the repository for longer, which is the failure the TTL exists to bound. The number is not the problem; renewing once is.
- Check the dispatch lease for the same shape - it has a 60s renewal TTL and the same once-per-pass renewal site.

eg9's logging is what made this legible: the refusal now names the holder ('run nobody'), which is how the slot's expiry could be read straight off the error rather than inferred.

Found by performing u9h, on the first run to reach a dispatched worker.
notes:
2026-09-21 06:49 - The cost of this is worse than a stuck run: the pass RETRIES, and a Workflow step retry re-executes the whole step callback - so every retry re-dispatches the worker, re-does the work, and fails the same publish.

Observed on run_2da1418005fe4c64bb9e15ca9e7b8fba:

    6:34:39  pass 1 starts, slot expires_at 6:37:38
    6:41:39  pass 1 publishes, refused, ERROR          (7 min, worker ran)
    6:41:49  slot re-acquired, pass 2 starts
    6:48:29  pass 2 publishes, refused                 (~7 min, worker ran again)

So the loop period is the length of a pass, and each turn of it spends a model doing work already done. Nothing in the feed says so - the run reads as 'starting' throughout (tick 991).

Two consequences for the fix:
1. The heartbeat is still the right fix, but the retry behaviour means a slot expiry is not merely a lost write, it is an unbounded redo. Worth a guard that refuses to re-dispatch a tick whose attempt branch already carries a completed attempt - the marker exists for exactly this, and adoption by identity is the local reconciler's answer to the same question.
2. Whatever the TTL becomes, a pass must not be able to silently repeat expensive work. The step boundary is in the wrong place if a retry means re-running a model.
2026-09-21 08:05 - The heartbeat this tick added is scaffolding, not foundation - see yoh. It exists only because a pass blocks for minutes, and a lease that must be beaten to be held is brittle by construction (operator, 2026-09-21: 'i don't want an architecture that relies on keep-alive'). When yoh lands and passes take seconds, remove the heartbeat and let the TTL stand unassisted. Keep eg9's reporting.
acceptance_criteria: A pass whose worker takes many minutes still holds a valid publish slot when it writes, proven by a test with a slow executor and a short TTL; a run that stops heartbeating still loses the slot
closed_reason: Landed via PR #24: the publish slot beats every TTL/3 while the pass runs, carrying a rotated token forward and stopping with the pass. Not a longer TTL - that is how long a dead run may wedge the repository. The retry-redoes-work hazard noted on this tick is NOT closed by it.
